packet.question: In QLoRA, distinguish the usual weight storage dtype, computation dtype, and which parameters receive weight gradients.

candidate_claims.text: In QLoRA, the usual weight storage dtype is 4-bit NormalFloat, the computation dtype is 16-bit BrainFloat, and only the LoRA parameters receive weight gradients.

evidence.quote: QLoRA has one low-precision storage data type, in our case usually 4-bit, and one computation data type that is usually BFloat16. In practice, this means whenever a QLoRA weight tensor is used, we dequantize the tensor to BFloat16, and then perform a matrix multiplication in 16-bit.

evidence.quote: To summarize, QLoRA has one storage data type (usually 4-bit NormalFloat) and a computation data type (16-bit BrainFloat).
